To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transient‐increased hepatic enhancement was observed in 8 of 8 patients with isolated right and left portal vein occlusions.

in eight of eight isolated right or left branch portal vein occlusion, transient‐increaased segmental hepatic parenchymal signal enhancement occurred on immediate postcontrast dynamic gadolinium MR images.

transient‐increased hepatic enhancement distally to a lobar portal vein obstruction is common on dynamic gadolininum‐enhanced gradient‐echo MR images and may be explained by increased hepatic arterial perfusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the transient hepatic enhancement in the liver distal to portal obstruction.
the use of dynamic MR imaging in patients with portal vein obstruction.
the study of transient‐increased hepatic segmental enhancement distally to portal vein obstruction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
transient‐increased enhancement of hepatic parenchyma distal to portal obstruction occurs in 100 percent of patients with right or left lobe portal vein obstruction.

transient increased segmental enhancement occurs in patients with isolated right and left portal vein obstruction and is due to increased hepataic arterial blood flow in patients with portal vein obstruction.
transient increased segmental enhancement is observed in eight of eight isolated right or left lobe portal vein obstruction, but is not observed in patients with main portal branch obstruction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

transient‐increased hepatic enhancement distally in the liver is seen on dynamic gadolininium‐enhanced gradient MR images in eight of eight (100%) patients with isolated right and left branch portal vein occlusion.
this finding should be considered normal in the presence of isolated right or left lobe portal vein obstruction.
the transient‐increased hepatic enhancement distally to portal vein obstruction is a common finding in patients with right or left portal lobar vein obstruction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transient‐increased enhancement distal to a portal vein obstruction is common on immediate postcontrast dynamic gadolinium FLASH images.

transient increased segmental enhancement is a relatively common phenomenon on dynamic MR images in patients with portal vein occlusion, and that this phenomenon may be used as a sign of portal vein occlusion.
the presence of transient increased enhancement distal to the site of portal vein obstruction is not pathognomonic of Budd‐Chiari syndrome.
